references.statement: The 10th bhava governs livelihood, rank, honour and karma; its lord's strength and placement set the career's trajectory.
The dashamsha (D10) refines the 10th-house promise: planets strong in D10 mark the arenas where public action succeeds.
Amala Yoga — a natural benefic in the 10th from Lagna or from Moon — is classically read as steady professional reputation that holds up over time, distinct from raw career success or wealth.
The 7th bhava and its lord, together with Venus as kalatra karaka, govern the spouse and the quality of the union; the navamsha (D9) confirms or withholds the rashi promise.

Manglik (Kuja) placements are classically read as a factor affecting marital harmony and timing, always alongside the classical cancellation rules (Mars in its own or exalted sign, Jupiter's aspect on Mars, Mars-Moon conjunction) — a flag to weigh, never a standalone verdict against marriage.

Venus as the natural karaka for marriage and relationship harmony is read alongside the 7th lord and house — a well-placed 7th house with an afflicted Venus (or vice versa) is a common classical pattern for a mixed marital picture, not a simple pass/fail.
The 6th bhava carries disease, debt and enemies together; afflictions to the 6th and its lord activate all three significations and must be separated by karaka and context.

The Lagna (1st bhava) and its lord govern overall vitality and constitution; a strong, undamaged Lagna lord is classically read as a baseline of resilience that other houses' afflictions play out against.

The 6th bhava and its lord are the primary reference for chronic and recurring illness; Saturn's involvement there is classically associated with slow-onset or long-duration conditions, Mars' involvement with acute, sudden onset — read as tendency, never as diagnosis.
The Atmakaraka (highest-degree graha) shows the soul's desire; its navamsha position (Karakamsha) frames the spiritual path and final direction.

The 12th bhava governs moksha (liberation), renunciation, and detachment from worldly bonds; the 9th governs dharma and guru connection — classical texts read the two together as part of the 'moksha trikona' axis with the 4th and 8th.
The Vimshamsha (D20) is examined specifically for spiritual practice (sadhana), devotion, and the nature of one's religious or ritual inclination — a finer lens than the 9th/12th houses alone.
The 2nd bhava shows accumulated wealth and family resources; the 11th shows income and gains. Dhana Yoga forms when the lords of these two houses associate, favouring material prosperity.

Dhana Yoga arises when the lords of the wealth houses (2nd, 5th, 9th, 11th) associate by conjunction, mutual aspect, or exchange; the association's strength and the lords' dignity set how much of the promise materializes.
Chandra-Mangal Yoga (Moon and Mars conjoined or opposed) is classically read as a driver of enterprising wealth-building — an active, self-made financial temperament rather than inherited ease.

The 4th bhava governs basic schooling and foundational learning; the 5th governs higher intellect, specialized study, and academic merit. The Chaturvimshamsha (D24) refines which field of learning and how much of the promise the native actually pursues.
Saraswati Yoga — Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each well-placed from Lagna with Jupiter strong — is the classical marker for articulate, wide-ranging learning and refined intellect.

Mercury's strength and dignity are read as one of the most consistent indicators of ease in formal education; an afflicted or debilitated Mercury is a common thread in charts with schooling breaks or difficulty, though never a standalone verdict.

The 5th bhava and its lord, together with Jupiter as the naisargika putrakaraka (natural significator of children), govern progeny — timing, number, and relationship; the Saptamsha (D7) is examined specifically for children's promise.

In the Jaimini scheme, the Putrakaraka (PK, the chara karaka for children) adds a second, planet-specific lens on progeny alongside the fixed 5th-house/Jupiter reading — the two should be read together, not substituted for each other.

Afflictions to the 5th house or its lord are read as timing/ease factors for conceiving and raising children, not as a fixed verdict — classical texts pair every affliction with cancellation and remedial factors.
The 4th bhava governs mother, home, land, vehicles, and general domestic comfort; the Chaturthamsha (D4) is examined specifically for fixed property and real-estate fortune.

The 3rd bhava shows younger siblings and courage; the 9th shows elder siblings, father, and fortune more broadly — classical texts read both houses together for the full sibling picture, not the 3rd alone.
The Dwadashamsha (D12) is examined for parents and ancestral lineage specifically — a finer lens than the 4th/9th houses alone for questions about parental welfare and inherited patterns.

The 12th bhava governs foreign residence and life far from one's birthplace; the 9th governs long journeys and fortune connected to distant places. Classical texts read both together for questions of relocation and life abroad, not the 12th in isolation.

Rahu is the planet most consistently associated with foreign lands, unconventional geography, and emigration in classical and modern practice alike; its house placement and dignity are read for the flavour and timing of foreign connection.
The 3rd bhava governs short journeys and everyday travel, distinct from the 9th/12th's longer-distance and foreign-residence significations — a chart can show ease in one register without the other.

The 6th bhava governs open enemies, disputes, and litigation; the 12th governs hidden losses and confinement. A strong 6th lord is classically read as an advantage in contested matters, while a weak or afflicted 6th lord favours settlement over confrontation.

Vipareeta Raja Yoga (a dusthana lord placed in a dusthana) is classically read as turning apparent obstruction into eventual advantage; in litigation contexts this is sometimes cited as a pattern for prevailing after early difficulty, though that is an interpretive extension rather than the yoga's primary classical scope.

The Lagna (ascendant) and its lord govern physical constitution and core temperament — how the self meets and engages with the world; the lord's strength and placement colour confidence, resilience, and self-expression.

The Moon governs the mind and emotional responsiveness — the instinctive, feeling nature beneath the Lagna's outward temperament. Its sign, house, and aspects shape how emotions are processed and expressed.

A Pancha Mahapurusha yoga forms when Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or Saturn occupies its own or exaltation sign in a kendra from the Lagna; each is classically read as a distinct, well-defined strength — courage, intellect, wisdom, refinement, or discipline respectively — rather than a generic boost.

Kemadruma dosha (no planets in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and none conjunct it) is classically read as a tendency toward emotional self-reliance or a sense of isolation — a flag to work with, like any dosha, not a fixed deficiency in someone's character.
A strong 10th lord — exalted, or in its own rashi or navamsha — gives fame and accomplished deeds; the same verse ties this to happiness from the father.
A 10th lord devoid of strength brings obstruction in one's work.
The 10th lord with a benefic, or placed in an auspicious house, gives gain through institutional patronage and through business; the contrary placement gives the contrary result.

Fame is indicated by the Moon in the 10th with the 10th lord in a trine from the 10th and the lagna lord in an angle from the lagna; also by the 11th lord in the 10th while a strong 10th lord receives Jupiter's aspect.
The 10th lord in the 10th makes one skilful in all kinds of work.
The dasha of the 10th lord brings recognition and award from the governing authority — read in a modern chart as institutional recognition, office or promotion.

The 10th bhava is the house of karma — acts and deeds — and carries the father alongside profession; several 10th-lord placements speak to the father rather than to work, so a 10th-house judgement should not be reduced to livelihood alone.

source.location: ch.21 v.2 and ch.24 v.114, pp.137,149 (Santhanam trans.)

references.statement: The 6th bhava governs disease, and ulcers or bruises of the body.
The 6th lord in the 6th, the lagna or the 8th indicates ulcers or bruises on the body; the sign falling in the 6th indicates which limb is concerned.

When a karaka or a bhava lord joins the 6th lord or occupies the 6th or 8th, the affliction indicated belongs to the relative that karaka signifies, not to the native — the governing frame of this rule is relatives, not a body-map of the reader.
The 6th lord in the lagna tends to a sickly constitution, alongside prominence and friction with one's own people.
The dasha of the 6th lord brings ill health and trouble from adversaries; the dashas of the 11th and 12th lords likewise carry a susceptibility to disease.

Across the twelve placements of the 6th lord only two speak to sickness; the remainder concern temperament, relationships and expenditure. The 6th lord signifies conflict and outlay at least as much as illness, so not every 6th-lord placement is a health statement.

Where a dasha lord sits by drekkana sets when inside the period its effects are felt — first drekkana at the commencement, second in the middle, third at the end — and retrogradation reverses that order, so the ever-retrograde nodes are always reversed. This is emphasis within the period, never a boundary on it.

A dasha runs favourably when its lord is in the lagna, exalted, in its own sign or a friend's sign at the period's commencement, and adversely when the lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated, or in an inimical sign.

Dignity and placement override a planet's natural benefic or malefic character for its dasha: a malefic exalted and in a good house does not give adverse results, while a benefic debilitated and in an inauspicious house does.

The 2nd and 7th lords are counted among the marakas, but their dashas are not read as distress alone: the 2nd is the house of wealth and a well-placed 2nd lord gives definite gain in its period, and the 7th indicates marriage, so a well-placed 7th lord brings auspicious celebration.
references.observance_note: Stated by the translator against a flat reading of the same chapter's own list. Recorded because reducing a 2nd- or 7th-lord dasha to distress misreads the source.

references.statement: Whether the lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give adverse results in their dashas is disputed within the text itself: ch.34 states that they do, while the ch.48 commentary holds from practice that they do not when placed in the 3rd, 6th and 11th respectively in their own signs.

source.location: ch.34 and ch.48 commentary, p.466 (Santhanam trans.)

references.observance_note: A genuine intra-text conflict, left unresolved. State which reading is being used rather than implying the text speaks with one voice.

references.statement: A strong, well-placed Jupiter in this 6th/8th-lord-in-lagna configuration tends to protect against illness — a positive constitutional signal, not a caution.

This configuration with Mercury indicates a constitutional tendency toward Pitta/bilious-type sensitivity — digestive and metabolic — read as a susceptibility, not a diagnosis, the same way a dosha is a flag rather than a verdict.
This configuration with Saturn indicates a constitutional tendency toward Vata/windy-type sensitivity — joints, nerves, mobility — read as a susceptibility, not a diagnosis.

This configuration with the Moon indicates a constitutional tendency toward Kapha/phlegmatic-type sensitivity — respiratory and fluid balance. Only this clause of the Moon's line is kept; a separate 'danger through water' phrase in the same verse is too ambiguous to state responsibly and is dropped.

source.location: ch.17 v.9-12½ (Moon clause, phlegmatic only), p.115 (Santhanam trans.)

references.observance_note: Only the phlegmatic/Kapha clause is used; the verse's separate water-danger phrase is excluded as too ambiguous to ground responsibly.

references.statement: This configuration with Mars indicates a tendency toward injury, wounds, or accident-proneness — a materially different claim from disease susceptibility, and the direct classical answer to whether a chart shows accident risk.
The 8th lord placed in the lagna indicates a general vulnerability to injury or wounding. The verse's separate clause about religious hostility is unrelated to health and is not carried over.

The 8th lord placed in the 6th house indicates a general susceptibility to illness (unnamed in the verse). The same shloka carries a childhood-danger clause and a separate clause on the closed topic documented for the 8th house generally (see health_kb_bphs_6th_house.md) -- neither is carried over here.
The ascendant lord placed in a sign of Mars or Mercury and aspected by Mercury is classically read as a caution toward the facial area -- worth attending to, not a diagnosis of a specific condition.

Mars or Mercury owning the ascendant and joining the Moon, Rahu or Saturn is classically read as a caution toward skin and immune-system vulnerability -- a signal historically taken seriously enough to warrant particular care, not a named diagnosis. The verse's own named condition is a specific, now-stigmatizing historical term and is deliberately not repeated; the underlying combinatorial signal (skin/immune area, worth checking) is what is kept.
references.observance_note: The verse names a specific historical disease term across three variants (by planet). Reframed to the body-system area the verse itself is organized around, dropping the stigmatizing specific name; this is a deliberate softening, stated so the boundary is visible rather than implied.

references.statement: The lords of the 6th and 8th conjunct the Sun in the ascendant is classically read as a caution toward febrile or inflammatory susceptibility -- general systemic wellbeing worth attending to during flare periods, not a named condition.
references.observance_note: The verse's second term (historically 'tumour', which in period medical English denoted any abnormal swelling, not specifically malignancy) is generalized to inflammatory/swelling susceptibility rather than read as a cancer-specific claim, since the source text does not support that specificity either way.

references.statement: The lords of the 6th and 8th conjunct Ketu in the ascendant is classically read as a caution toward the abdominal/digestive area -- worth attending to, not a named diagnosis.

Saturn with Rahu conjunct the 6th lord and 6th house, or Mars in the 6th with the 6th lord in the 8th, is classically read as flagging childhood as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution about a life-stage, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: The verse states specific ages (6 and 12) tied to specific named illnesses. Neither the age nor the illness name is carried over -- only the life-stage-level flag, for the same reason a marriage or children timing verse's literal age is not restated as a modern prediction: a specific year is a period artifact, and pairing it with a named illness is the clearest case of a medical verdict this corpus holds.

references.statement: The Moon in Sagittarius or Pisces with Jupiter in the 6th, Rahu in the 6th with the ascendant lord in the 8th and Mandi in an angle, or the 6th and 12th lords in exchange, are classically read as flagging youth and young adulthood as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: Same treatment as the childhood entry: the verse's named illnesses and specific ages (19, 22, 26) are not carried over, only the life-stage-level flag.

references.statement: Saturn and the Moon together in the 6th, or Saturn with an inimical planet as the ascendant lord occupies the ascendant, are classically read as flagging midlife and later years as a period warranting extra health vigilance -- a general caution, not a named condition or a specific age.
references.observance_note: Same treatment: the verse's named illnesses and specific ages (45, 59) are not carried over, only the life-stage-level flag.
